sections.h2: Which St. Louis County offices handle a property tax question?
sections.html:
Three county offices cover most questions, and all of them work from 41 South Central Avenue in Clayton, the county seat. The Assessor values real estate and personal property, the Board of Equalization hears value appeals, and the Collector of Revenue, part of the Department of Revenue, bills and collects.

St. Louis County property tax contacts (county website)

The Collector bills for more than 200 taxing districts, which is why two homes in the same city can receive very different totals. Read the district list on your bill line by line, because each line is a separate taxing body.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about St. Louis County itself?
sections.html:
St. Louis County is in eastern Missouri, bounded by the City of St. Louis and the Mississippi River on the east, the Missouri River on the north and the Meramec River on the south. It has 523 square miles, of which about 508 are land, and the 2020 census counted 1,004,125 people, the most of any Missouri county. The seat is Clayton and the largest city is Florissant (Wikipedia).

The District of St. Louis was renamed St. Louis County on October 1, 1812. The city and county separated in 1877, when voters in the City of St. Louis chose to become an independent city, and in the 1960s suburban growth pushed the county's population past the city's for the first time. The county has since grown into dozens of incorporated municipalities, from Kirkwood, Webster Groves, Ladue and Clayton to Ferguson, Hazelwood, Chesterfield, Wildwood and University City. It also has 23 public school districts, among them Rockwood, Parkway, Lindbergh, Mehlville, Pattonville, Ritenour and Ferguson-Florissant, so the school line on a tax bill varies widely.

On Census QuickFacts, the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 990,911 residents, 1.4% below the April 2020 base. The county has 448,637 housing units and 413,849 households. Owners hold 69.2% of homes, the median owned home was valued at $276,800 for 2020 to 2024, median gross rent was $1,209 and median household income was $82,936. The average commute is 23.1 minutes.

sections.h2: How often does the St. Louis County Assessor reassess a home?
sections.html:
Every odd-numbered year, state law requires the County Assessor to reassess all real estate in the county, according to the county reassessment page. The next reassessment is 2027.

The county site describes the office's aim as treating every owner fairly and giving clear, accurate and timely information. When a notice arrives, compare the value and the property class with what you know about the house, then decide whether to call the Assessor at 314-615-2555 before the appeal window closes. The Assessor answers value questions by phone on weekdays, while in-person visits run Monday through Thursday.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a St. Louis County valuation?
sections.html:
You appeal to the Board of Equalization, which is separate from the Assessor. The board hears value disputes for homeowners, businesses and manufacturers and also considers exemption requests from not-for-profit organizations. Contact it at 314-615-7195 or boe@stlouiscountymo.gov.

  • Deadline: state law, RSMo 137.275, requires the appeal to be lodged with the board on or before the second Monday in July. For 2026 that was July 13, now past. The next is July 12, 2027.
  • Method: the statute allows you to appeal in person, through an attorney or agent, or in writing.
  • Burden of proof: RSMo 138.060 says there is no presumption that the assessor's valuation is correct, and in a charter county with more than one million inhabitants the assessor must prove the value does not exceed true market value. The county counted 1,004,125 residents in 2020, so ask the board how that rule applies to your case.
  • Next step: the State Tax Commission hears appeals from the board's decision. Ask the board for its current filing instructions.

Bring a recent appraisal, a purchase contract, comparable sales or repair estimates to support a lower number.

sections.h2: When is St. Louis County property tax due, and what happens when it is late?
sections.html:
Penalties begin after January 1. RSMo 139.100 directs the Collector to collect a penalty on unpaid tax after the first day of January, using the amount in RSMo 140.100, which is 18% of each year's delinquency for land in the back tax book. For land redeemed before a sale, the penalty cannot exceed 2% per month or fraction of a month.

Mailing counts. The same statute treats a payment delivered by United States mail as paid on the postmark date, and certified or registered mail uses the registration date. If the postmark falls within the allowed period, no added tax or penalty applies. The Collector's page links to a Pay Taxes page, a tax rates lookup and a customer service portal at csportal.stlouiscountymo.gov.

The Collector's page also carries a 2026 tax bill update. It says the department is aware of issues affecting the accuracy of some bills, including those of owners approved for the senior tax freeze, and that bills had not been mailed when the notice was posted. Check that page before relying on an amount, and call 314-615-7100 if your bill looks wrong.

sections.h2: How does St. Louis County property tax affect a closing?
sections.html:
The county's tax bill is part of every closing here. Title companies ask for a payoff or proration for the current year, and an unpaid prior year carries the 18% penalty described above. Ask the Collector for the balance on your parcel, then give the figure to the closing agent.

If a lender pays your tax from escrow, confirm that the last bill was paid before you list. If a senior tax freeze is on your account and your bill is among those the county says it is correcting, keep the corrected statement with your closing papers, and ask the Collector how the freeze is treated when the property changes hands.

The Collector also handles the county's tax sale for delinquent parcels, a step the Collector's page lists among its duties. Owners who are behind should ask the Collector for payoff figures and sale dates at 314-615-7100 instead of waiting for a notice.

faqs.q: Where is the St. Louis County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: It is at 41 South Central Avenue, 3rd floor, Clayton, MO 63105. Call 314-615-2555 on weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, or visit Monday through Thursday from 8:00 to 3:30.

faqs.q: Who do I call to appeal a St. Louis County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Equalization at 314-615-7195 or email boe@stlouiscountymo.gov. The board is separate from the Assessor and hears appeals for homes, businesses and manufacturers.

faqs.q: What is the St. Louis County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: State law sets it at the second Monday in July. The 2026 date, July 13, has passed, and the next date is July 12, 2027. Appeals can be made in person, by an agent or attorney, or in writing.

faqs.q: Is the St. Louis County bill the same in every city?
faqs.a: No. The Collector bills for more than 200 taxing districts, and your school, library, fire and other districts decide most of the total. Two houses in different school districts can pay very different amounts.

faqs.q: What happens if I mail my St. Louis County payment on the last day?
faqs.a: Missouri law counts a payment mailed through the postal service as paid on the postmark date. Certified or registered mail uses the registration date. Keep the receipt and the stamped envelope.
